questions.question: How do you check your blind spot before changing lanes?

options.text: Look in the left side mirror.
Look in the right side mirror.
Look in the rearview mirror.
Look over your shoulder toward the direction you want to move.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your shoulder toward the direction you want to move.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move to check your blind spot.

questions.question: What happens when you drive while distracted?

options.text: It is never dangerous.
You react more slowly to hazards.
You usually drive faster.
It is only dangerous for young drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: You react more slowly to hazards.
questions.explanation: Distractions slow down how quickly you react to traffic and hazards. Distracted driving is never safe.

questions.question: What happens if you mix alcohol with prescription or over-the-counter medicine?

options.text: The medicine reduces the effect of the alcohol.
The alcohol helps the medicine cure a cold.
The combination can strengthen the effects of both substances.
There is no effect because they are different substances.

questions.correctAnswerText: The combination can strengthen the effects of both substances.
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol and other drugs increases how much both affect your body. For example, one drink with a cold medicine could affect you as much as several drinks alone.

questions.question: What is the best way to avoid hydroplaning?

options.text: Keep your tires properly maintained.
Slow down on wet or slushy roads.
Watch for standing water or puddles.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: On wet roads, your car takes longer to stop and may skid when turning. Do not use cruise control on wet or icy roads. Slow down and drive carefully.

questions.question: What can cause distracted driving?

options.text: Eating, drinking, or smoking.
Talking or texting on a cell phone.
Changing the radio or CD.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Drivers make about 200 decisions for every mile driven. It is important to focus all your attention on driving. Any extra task can be a dangerous distraction.

questions.question: You are borrowing an unfamiliar vehicle from a friend. What should you do?

options.text: Do not worry because all vehicles are the same.
Do not tell your friend you are unfamiliar with the vehicle.
Ignore any obvious problems to avoid embarrassing your friend.
Take a few minutes to learn where all the controls are and how to use them before driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a few minutes to learn where all the controls are and how to use them before driving.
questions.explanation: Before driving an unfamiliar vehicle, learn the location and operation of the turn signals, hazard lights, headlights, windshield wipers, brakes, gear selector, and horn. Fix any problems before driving.

questions.question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning?

options.text: Do not speed on wet roads.
Keep your tires filled to the correct air pressure.
Replace tires with worn tread.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when your vehicle slides on a layer of water between your tires and the road. Low tire pressure and worn tread increase hydroplaning risk. Speeding also increases the risk.

questions.question: Your wheels slip off the edge of the road. What should you do?

options.text: Jerk the steering wheel to force the vehicle back onto the pavement.
Speed up and steer back onto the pavement slowly.
Brake hard and stop.
Gently brake. Turn the wheel to get back on the pavement at a safe speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gently brake. Turn the wheel to get back on the pavement at a safe speed.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle leaves the road, keep your wheels off the pavement and reduce speed by braking gently. When you are going slow enough, turn the wheel to return to the pavement. Do not jerk the steering wheel sharply.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road ahead curves only to the right.
The road ahead turns sharply to the right.
The road ahead curves to the right, then to the left.
The road ahead curves to the left, then to the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead curves to the right, then to the left.
questions.explanation: Warning signs alert drivers to hazards ahead and are yellow with black markings. This sign warns that the road ahead curves right and then left.

questions.question: When entering a roundabout, you must slow down and yield to whom?

options.text: Vehicles in the roundabout.
Bicyclists in the roundabout.
Pedestrians in the roundabout.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: When entering a roundabout, yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and vehicles already in the roundabout.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A community group is picking up trash on the highway ahead.
Workers are on or near the road in the work zone ahead.
Children are playing ahead.
There is a pedestrian crosswalk ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Workers are on or near the road in the work zone ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that workers may be on or near the road ahead. Drive with extra care through this area.

questions.question: You are driving on a divided multilane highway and see or hear an emergency vehicle coming. What should you do?

options.text: Ignore the signal if other lanes are open for the emergency vehicle.
Stop as fast as you can.
Slow down, move to give the emergency vehicle a clear path, and stop.
Speed up to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, move to give the emergency vehicle a clear path, and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights, slow down, make room for the emergency vehicle, and stop. Do not try to speed away from it.

questions.question: How can you help prevent rear-end collisions?

options.text: Avoid sudden stops.
Check your mirrors and blind spots before stopping.
Release the gas pedal to slow down before using the brakes.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Sudden stops make it hard for drivers behind you to avoid hitting you. Release the gas pedal first to slow down, then apply the brakes smoothly. This activates your brake lights and gives other drivers time to react.

questions.question: When passing other vehicles, you should:

options.text: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
Honk your horn at least three times.
Move back into your lane within 10 feet of the car you passed.
You do not need to signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
questions.explanation: Before passing, check your mirrors and blind spots. Use your turn signal before changing lanes. Move back into your lane only when you can see the front of the other car in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: You must always signal when:

options.text: Changing lanes.
Pulling into or out of a parking space.
Pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Always signal when changing lanes, pulling into or out of a parking space, or pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area. Signals let other drivers know what you are doing and help prevent accidents.

questions.question: When you see a steady green traffic light, you should:

options.text: Keep driving, unless vehicles or pedestrians are already in the intersection.
Stop if a police officer is nearby.
Treat it like a four-way stop.
Come to a complete stop first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep driving, unless vehicles or pedestrians are already in the intersection.
questions.explanation: At a green light, yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and any vehicles still in the intersection. You can keep driving, but slow down in case the light changes before you reach the intersection.

questions.question: You must stop at a railroad crossing when:

options.text: A flagger directs you to stop.
There is a stop sign.
Flashing red lights and gates are present and working.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger tells you to, when there is a stop sign, or when flashing red lights and gates are present and working.

questions.question: If another driver cuts you off, you should:

options.text: Pull beside them and yell.
Let it go.
Flash your high beams.
Cut them off in return.

questions.explanation: To avoid road rage, do not take it personally if another driver cuts you off. Just let it go and keep driving safely.

questions.question: Before you start the car, you should:

options.text: Make sure only back seat passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure only adult passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure only child passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure all passengers have buckled their seat belts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure all passengers have buckled their seat belts.
questions.explanation: Develop a habit of buckling your seat belt and checking that all passengers do the same before you start the car.

questions.question: Do not pass in these situations:

options.text: On a hill or curve.
When school bus lights are flashing.
When approaching an intersection.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Never pass if you cannot see oncoming traffic, on hills or curves, at intersections, before or on railroad crossings or bridges, or in any no passing zone. Do not pass a stopped school bus with flashing red lights unless you are on the opposite side of a divided road with a median.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: There is a detour ahead.
You must stop for flaggers.
The road ahead is closed to traffic.
Road work is happening on the highway ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road work is happening on the highway ahead.
questions.explanation: Orange signs warn drivers about construction and maintenance work. This sign tells you that a work zone is ahead. Slow down and drive carefully.

questions.question: You are in an accident. What should you do?

options.text: Stop immediately.
Help the injured.
Call the police.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Stop your vehicle right away. Move it out of traffic if you can. Call the police and ask for an ambulance if needed. Do not move injured people unless necessary. Apply direct pressure to stop heavy bleeding. Wait for emergency help to arrive.

questions.question: Seat belts work best when worn by:

options.text: The driver only.
Passengers on long drives.
Everyone on expressways.
Everyone in the car every time it is driven.

questions.correctAnswerText: Everyone in the car every time it is driven.
questions.explanation: All people in your car should wear a seat belt every time you drive. Without a seat belt, a person can become a projectile in a crash and hurt others in the car.

questions.question: What commonly causes traffic accidents?

options.text: Not paying attention while driving
Driving too fast for the conditions
Following other vehicles too closely
All of the above

questions.explanation: Speeding is a major cause of crashes. Not paying attention can cause you to hit other vehicles. Most rear-end collisions happen because drivers follow too closely.

questions.question: When driving on highways, you should:

options.text: Stay alert.
Keep your eyes moving.
Be ready to react to hazards.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Stay alert on highways and be ready for unexpected hazards. Do not stare at one thing for more than a few seconds. This prevents highway hypnosis.

questions.question: Which statement about speed is correct?

options.text: Driving too slowly on some highways can be dangerous.
Speeding can kill.
Speeding is safe if you are a skilled driver.
Both driving too slowly on some highways can be dangerous and speeding can kill.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both driving too slowly on some highways can be dangerous and speeding can kill.
questions.explanation: As speed increases, the chance of death in a crash increases. At speeds above 80 miles per hour, survival in a crash is unlikely. Driving much slower than other traffic is also dangerous because other drivers may take risky actions to pass you.

questions.question: A pedestrian starts to cross in front of you. What should you do?

options.text: Flash your lights.
Slow down.
Speed up and pass the pedestrian.
Stop and let the pedestrian cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrian cross.
questions.explanation: Slow down when you see pedestrians. Be extra careful near children. Always let pedestrians cross in a crosswalk.

questions.question: You miss your exit on an interstate. What should you do?

options.text: Stop and make a U-turn.
Get off at the next exit and return to the missed exit.
Ask the driver next to you for help.
Back up on the highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get off at the next exit and return to the missed exit.
questions.explanation: Do not back up or turn around on the highway. Go to the next exit and safely turn around.

questions.question: At night, what is hardest to see?

options.text: Road signs.
Pedestrians.
Other vehicles.
Street lights.

questions.explanation: Pedestrians are harder to see at night than signs and other roadside objects.

questions.question: If you take an over-the-counter drug, what should you do?

options.text: Read the label before driving.
Drink alcohol instead.
Drive regardless of warning labels.
Drive only during the day.

questions.explanation: Over-the-counter drugs like cold and allergy medicine can affect your driving. Always check the label for warnings. Ask your doctor or pharmacist if you are unsure about driving while taking medication.

questions.question: If you are in a serious car crash, what should you do?

options.text: Stop.
Call the police.
Check if anyone is injured.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: If you crash, stop your vehicle and move it off the road if possible. If anyone is hurt, call 911 and help them. You must report the crash to police if someone is injured, someone dies, or there is more than $1,000 in property damage.

questions.question: If a flagger is directing traffic in a construction zone, you must:

options.text: Follow the flagger's directions.
Do what other cars are doing, even if the flagger says otherwise.
Assume the flagger should not be there.
Follow normal traffic laws as if there is no construction.

questions.explanation: Slow down and follow directions from flaggers, signs, and police officers in construction zones. Not following them is illegal and dangerous to construction workers.

questions.question: What do two solid yellow lines on the road mean?

options.text: Both directions can pass.
No one can pass.
You can pass at the top of a hill.
You can pass during the day.

questions.explanation: Yellow lines mean traffic is moving in opposite directions. Never cross two solid yellow lines to pass from either direction.

questions.question: A driver entering public traffic from a driveway or private road:

options.text: Has the right-of-way.
Must let drivers on the public road go first.
Can force their way into traffic.
Can assume other drivers will move for them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must let drivers on the public road go first.
questions.explanation: When entering traffic from a driveway or private road, you must yield to cars already on the public road. Merge safely when you have space.

questions.question: What should you do with loose objects in your car?

options.text: Put them on the back seat.
Put them on the dashboard.
Secure them to prevent hazards.
Keep them on a back shelf.

questions.explanation: Loose objects can fly around inside your car during a crash and hurt people. Do not put heavy or sharp items on the dashboard or rear shelf.

questions.question: When you see a railroad crossing warning sign, you should:

options.text: Drive faster than the train.
Be ready to stop if a train is near.
Go around lowered gates.
Assume no train is coming and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop if a train is near.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossing warning signs alert you that a train may be nearby. Always obey these signs and barriers. Never drive around lowered gates.

questions.question: When driving on wet roads, remember:

options.text: Roads are slippery right after rain starts.
Wet roads can cause your car to slide.
Leave extra distance before stopping.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Wet roads are very slippery, especially when rain just starts. Your tires lose grip on the wet surface. Slow down and increase your stopping distance on wet roads.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: No right turn.
You must turn right.
Watch for traffic on your right.
Don't park on the right side.

questions.explanation: A red circle with a line through it means the action is not allowed. In this case, no right turns are permitted.

questions.question: If you are in an accident, you should:

options.text: Stop at or near the scene.
Stay out of traffic lanes.
Turn off the engines of damaged vehicles.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: You must stop at or near the crash scene. Move your vehicle out of traffic if possible. Do not stand in traffic lanes as other cars could hit you. Turn off the engines of wrecked vehicles.

questions.question: What do double solid yellow lines down the middle of the road mean?

options.text: Railroad crossing ahead.
Pedestrian crossing ahead.
No one can pass from either direction.
Both directions can pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: No one can pass from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean no passing is allowed from either direction. You can only cross them to turn left or pass pedestrians, bicyclists, or scooter riders when the other lane is clear and safe.
